title: Local pure-tensor normalization of the canonical étale scalar comparisons
statement:
Let $e:U\to V$ be an etale morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-etale-morphism], and let $\varphi:A\to B$ be a unital map of commutative rings in $\mathrm{Type}(u+1)$. Use ordinary constant-ring module sheaves on the small etale sites [def-weil-pbc-etale-sheaves]. Write $S_R$ for sheafified sum extension [def-weil-pbc-etale-sum-extension], $e_R^*$ for geometric inverse image and $c_R:e_R^*\cong\mathrm{Res}_{\iota_e}$ for its restriction identification [lem-weil-pbc-etale-inverse-image-restriction], and $E_T\dashv\mathrm{Res}_{\varphi,T}$ for scalar extension/restriction [def-sf-etale-sheaf-scalar-extension]. Let $r:\mathrm{Res}_{\varphi,V};e_A^*\cong e_B^*;\mathrm{Res}_{\varphi,U}$ be the specified comparison from uniqueness of left adjoints to direct image/coextension [lem-sbc-canonical-restrict-scalars-functor-comparisons], and let $a:E_V;e_B^*\cong e_A^*;E_U$ be the specified scalar/pullback comparison [def-pur-scalar-pullback-representative-data]. Define $q:S_A;E_V\cong E_U;S_B$ by uniqueness of left adjoints for $(S_A\dashv e_A^*);(E_V\dashv\mathrm{Res}_{\varphi,V})$ and $(E_U\dashv\mathrm{Res}_{\varphi,U});(S_B\dashv e_B^*)$, transporting the latter right adjoint along $r^{-1}$. Use ordinary sheaf tensor [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product] and the fixed sum sections $i_W$, lift sections $\ell_W$, scalar pure sections $t_T$, and coefficient pullback $\kappa:e_A^*B_V\cong B_U$ [def-pur-etale-projection-data, def-sp-etale-scalar-section-data]. For every $A$-module sheaf $H$ on $U$, every etale test object $W$ over $U$, $x\in H(W)$ and $b\in B_V(eW)$,
$$q_H(eW)\bigl(t_V(i_W(x),b)\bigr)=i_W\bigl(t_U(x,\kappa_W(\ell_W(b)))\bigr).$$
For every $A$-module sheaf $F$ on $V$, the same $W$, $x\in F(eW)$ and $b\in B_V(eW)$,
$$a_F^{-1}(W)\bigl(t_U(\ell_W(x),\kappa_W(\ell_W(b)))\bigr)=\ell_W\bigl(t_V(x,b)\bigr).$$
These are only local normalization formulas for constructed canonical comparisons; no fold-counit or cochain identity is assumed. The coefficients are arbitrary local sections of the constant coefficient sheaf. No separation, quasi-compactness, finiteness, or flatness is required.

proof.text: Identify geometric inverse image along e with restriction of test objects by upperStarIsoLocalizationRestriction. Restriction of scalars commutes strictly with this restriction. Transporting that identity through the two inverse-image isomorphisms gives upperStarRestrictScalarsIsoSheaf: apply uniqueness of left adjoints to the restriction/coextension adjunction and geometric adjunction, and verify equality of their units using sectionwise unit naturality. The private helper localization_scalar_comparison proves this bridge in the attached module: equality of composite adjunctions follows from the coextension-unit naturality, and leftAdjointUniq_trans finishes the comparison.

source.place: Tags 03S3 and 03S4, localization and explicit sum adjunction

proof.text: The unit equation for left-adjoint uniqueness gives q(η_V(i_W(m)))=i_W(η_U(m)). Write the scalar tensor map as η tensored with the coefficient sheaf, then the lax tensorator of restriction of scalars, then the right unitor. These operations commute with restriction and with the sum unit. Equivalently extend the summandwise pairing (i_W(m),b)↦i_W(m⊗b|W) through sheafification. Bilinear sheafification uniqueness identifies that extension with q. This proves its formula for arbitrary local coefficient sections, not just constant scalars.

source.place: Tags 03S3 and 03S4 with sites-modules.tex Tag 0GMW, extension of bilinear pairings through sheafification

proof.text: The scalar/pullback comparison is the inverse scalar mate of the same restriction identity. Its unit equation applied to the scalar tensor pairing gives the second formula. The coefficient factor is upperStarRestrictScalarsIsoSheaf at the unit object followed by the inverse monoidal unit comparison, hence is exactly compactificationCoefficientPullbackIso. The inverse-image tensor comparison preserves pure tensors, and naturality extends the equation through sheafification. Empty tests and zero rings obey the same linear identities.

lean.statement:
theorem etaleSumScalarIso_tensorSections
    {A B : Type (u + 1)} [CommRing A] [CommRing B]
    (φ : A →+* B) {U V : Scheme.{u}} (e : U ⟶ V) [Etale e] :
      (∀ (H : Sheaf U.smallEtaleTopology (ModuleCat.{u + 1} A)) (W : U.Etale)
        (x : H.obj.obj (op W))
        (b : (scalarCoefficientSheaf φ V).obj.obj
          (op ((MorphismProperty.Over.map ⊤ (inferInstance : Etale e)).obj W))),
        ((etaleSumScalarIso φ e).hom.app H).hom.app
            (op ((MorphismProperty.Over.map ⊤ (inferInstance : Etale e)).obj W))
            (compactificationScalarTensorSection φ _
              ((MorphismProperty.Over.map ⊤ (inferInstance : Etale e)).obj W)
              (etaleSumSection A e H W x) b) =
          etaleSumSection B e ((ProEtale.etaleSheafExtendScalars φ U).obj H) W
            (compactificationScalarTensorSection φ H W x
              ((compactificationCoefficientPullbackIso φ e).hom.hom.app (op W)
                (etaleLiftSection A e (scalarCoefficientSheaf φ V) W b)))) ∧
      (∀ (F : Sheaf V.smallEtaleTopology (ModuleCat.{u + 1} A)) (W : U.Etale)
        (x : F.obj.obj
          (op ((MorphismProperty.Over.map ⊤ (inferInstance : Etale e)).obj W)))
        (b : (scalarCoefficientSheaf φ V).obj.obj
          (op ((MorphismProperty.Over.map ⊤ (inferInstance : Etale e)).obj W))),
        ((scalarSheafPullbackIso φ e).inv.app F).hom.app (op W)
            (compactificationScalarTensorSection φ _ W (etaleLiftSection A e F W x)
              ((compactificationCoefficientPullbackIso φ e).hom.hom.app (op W)
                (etaleLiftSection A e (scalarCoefficientSheaf φ V) W b))) =
          etaleLiftSection B e ((ProEtale.etaleSheafExtendScalars φ V).obj F) W
            (compactificationScalarTensorSection φ F
              ((MorphismProperty.Over.map ⊤ (inferInstance : Etale e)).obj W) x b))
lean.note: etaleSumScalarIso is constructed solely from adjunction uniqueness. Private tensor_section_map, restrict_tensor_section and scalar_tensor_section prove the elementary local pairing calculus; localization_scalar_comparison proves that the geometric coefficient square is strict restriction in test-object coordinates. Only the two stated local tensor normalization identities remain sorry.
